text:
maya: Heads up — running into weird behavior when we try to move tenant namespaces from hosted GPU pools to dedicated-preemptible pools. Pods get scheduled, then a node is reclaimed and some pods go into Terminating for >10m and block scale-down. Anyone seen this exact interaction with CA + preemptible eviction hooks?

juan: yeah saw that last week. usually two things: PDBs holding pods, and PV detach waiting causing Terminating. but CA still marks node as empty if all pods tolerated the taint? confusing.

maya: example flow: create pod with toleration for preemptible-taint, start job (local scratch), node preempts, node is gone in cloud console, pod stays Terminating. CA doesn't reclaim resource because cloud provider shows node deleted but k8s still waiting on kubelet finalizers.

infra-bot: [node-event] node/np-gpu-preempt-7 - Instance terminated by provider (preemptible). Notified autoscaler.

juan: two quick checks: 1) are pods using emptyDir or hostPath? emptyDir needs kubelet node evacuation; 2) are we running finalizers (like CSI detach) that time out?

maya: emptyDir yes, and we don't use CSI for those tenants. it's mostly transient batch tasks but some have traces that need graceful cleanup.

sara: cost angle: preemptible dedicated pools are much cheaper but we can't have long tail Terminating pods delaying autoscaler for hours. i propose a short eviction-policy TTL for these namespaces + a sidecar that checkpoints to S3 within 30s. then fallback to hosted if checkpoint missing.

juan: agree on TTL. also consider using node.kubernetes.io/preemptible taint + a mandatory toleration only for pods that are checkpointed. Otherwise don't schedule tenant critical services there. Example toleration/taint pattern:```yaml
# node taint
kubectl taint nodes np-gpu-preempt-7 preemptible=true:NoExecute
# pod toleration
tolerations:
- key: \"preemptible\"
  operator: \"Equal\"
  value: \"true\"
  effect: \"NoExecute\"
  tolerationSeconds: 60
```

liam: careful: tolerationSeconds only controls eviction on the node; if node disappears (provider preempt), pods go to Terminating and cloud provider detach can block. We had good results with 3 parts: priorityClass (low), tolerationSeconds small, and a termination-sidecar that calls `kubectl delete --grace-period=0 --force` after checkpointing.

maya: about namespace binding: is it better to use NamespaceSelector on podAffinity or rely on dedicated nodePools with nodeSelector? I hate label proliferation on every pod.

juan: prefer nodeSelector at Deployment level for long-running infra. For tenant-initiated workloads (self-serve), use a namespace-level annotation + mutating webhook that injects nodeSelector/tolerations on admission. That keeps manifests clean.

sara: +1 to webhook. also add a quota so a namespace can't eat the whole preemptible pool. we need soft limits and a burst policy to fall back to hosted if preemptible saturates.

liam: CA config note: set scaleDown.unneededTime to something like 3m for preemptible node groups and tune maxCombinedPerNode to avoid eviction storms. Also ensure cloud provider's instance-termination hook triggers PodDisruptionBudget-aware eviction controller; otherwise use a controller that marks pods with an annotation so we can prioritize migration.

maya: action items I hear: 1) juan -> prototype mutating webhook to inject tolerations/nodeSelector for preemptible-dedicated namespaces (due EOD Friday). 2) liam -> CA tune proposal for preemptible nodegroup (unneededTime=3m, maxPodEviction=10) 3) sara -> cost/runbook: checkpoint-sidecar template and fallback routing policy to hosted pools. 4) infra-bot -> add alert when >2 nodes with Terminating pods older than 5m in any dedicated-preemptible pool.

juan: noted. will link a PoC repo in #eng-infra when ready.

sara: thanks — also add a short runbook snippet for SRE on forced-drain (forceDelete flow).

liam: :thumbsup:

maya: thanks everyone, will test with the nightly tenant migration jobs and report back.
